newsitem.title: INDIA: Cricket-India in good heart for forthcoming test series.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-India in good heart for forthcoming test series.

text.p: India's victory over fancied South Africa in the Titan Cup limited overs final ended a year-long drought for the side and boosted the team's morale for the test series ahead.
"Our team has been improving day by day. We have been able to put our act together in the last two matches.
"I think this should augur well for the forthcoming test series," said India captain Sachin Tendulkar.
India will play three tests against South Africa, the first beginning in Ahmedabad on November 20.
A week ago the talented Indians overcame poor form to pull off a remarkable last-over victory over Australia in the triangular series to qualify for the final.
South Africa won all six preliminary matches, including three against India, in their run-up to the final.
India's previous victory in a one-day series was more than a year ago when they clinched the Asia Cup in Sharjah.
A series of upsets and controversies followed.

India performed poorly during a tour of England, under Mohammed Azharuddin's captaincy. Opener Navjot Sidhu walked out of the tour, largely because of his differences with Azharuddin who subseqently lost the captaincy.
Tendulkar's elevation as skipper came sooner than expected but the team's performance in the one-day series in Sri Lanka and Canada had been unimpressive.
Much was expected of the Indian team in the three-nation Titan triangular series at home as both Australia and South Africa arrived in India without some of their leading players.
India's problems in finding a sound opener persisted. Sidhu's suspension from the team for walking out of the England tour brought to the fore the problem of finding an opening partner for Tendulkar.

But India came off better in two matches against the Australians who were without leg spinner Shane Warne. The third game between the two teams was washed out, leaving Australia with only one point in the tournament.

Judging from the way the South African juggernaut rolled, a victory for them in the final against India appeared a mere formality, even though their skipper Hansie Cronje maintained it would not be an easy task.
"They (the Indians) are a highly talented side and could be at their best at the most unexpected time," he said on the eve of the final.
His statement was almost like a prediction.
However, despite their victory over a side boasting 25 wins in 29 one-day matches this year, India are fully aware that the forthcoming test series will prove to be the real testing ground for them.
